key_insight: ApexGO is a generative AI system that redesigns peptide antibiotics to improve killing of drug‑resistant bacteria; candidates validated in vitro and in mouse infection models matched or outperformed standard antibiotics.
problem_solved: Addresses the urgent need for new, effective antimicrobial agents by enabling rapid, targeted optimization of peptide antibiotics against drug‑resistant pathogens.
method: Generative model trained on peptide sequences and activity data to propose redesigned antimicrobial peptides (ApexGO).
In silico filtering for potency and safety followed by experimental validation: lab assays (MIC, kill curves) and mouse infection models.
Iterative design–test loop that refines candidates based on experimental feedback to optimize efficacy and tolerability.
impact: Shows that generative models can produce therapeutically relevant peptide candidates and close the loop between computational design and experimental validation, accelerating antibiotic discovery workflows for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data → generative model (ApexGO) → candidate filtering → in vitro assays → mouse efficacy
Bar chart comparing antimicrobial potency of ApexGO-designed peptides vs standard antibiotics (e.g., MIC or survival rates)
Sequence/feature visualization (sequence logo or heatmap) highlighting the design changes that correlate with improved activity
Icon set: bacteria, petri dish, mouse, and AI/brain to convey cross-disciplinary validation
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
